explanations.answer: They cry out to Jesus for mercy
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (Matthew 20:30). They didn't whisper it or hint at it. I think these two knew a chance when they heard one, and they used their voices.

explanations.answer: They wait quietly for Him to pass
explanations.explanation: Quiet would have been the safe play, friend. But the text says they cried out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (Matthew 20:30). Waiting quietly is how I spent my first years in that drawer, and it got me a lot of dust. These two chose the opposite.

explanations.answer: They try to push through the crowd
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, but the text never says they moved at all. They were sitting beside the road, and when they heard Jesus was passing by, they cried out (Matthew 20:30). Pushing through a crowd takes eyes and elbows. These two used the one thing they could aim straight at Him, their voices.

Right, baker. "The crowd admonished them to be silent" (Matthew 20:31). That's a whole crowd telling two men to pipe down. Imagine trying to shout your order at a counter while the whole line goes "shhhh."

Not quite, friend. Jericho was the city behind them, since the crowd was leaving it (Matthew 20:29). The crowd didn't send the men anywhere. Matthew says the crowd admonished them to be silent (Matthew 20:31).

Nice guess, but tomorrow never comes up. The text says the crowd admonished them to be silent (Matthew 20:31). The crowd wanted the noise to stop right then. I'll say it plain: nobody offered these two a better time.

explanations.answer: They cry out all the louder
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. "…they cried out all the louder, 'Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!'" (Matthew 20:31). The crowd said hush, and they turned the volume up. I wish I'd had that kind of nerve when somebody first slid that drawer shut on me.

I get why you'd pick it, friend. A whole crowd telling you to be quiet is a lot of pressure. But Matthew says they "cried out all the louder" (Matthew 20:31). Quiet was the one thing they refused to do.

explanations.answer: They walk away down the road
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't have them going anywhere, baker. It says they "cried out all the louder, 'Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!'" (Matthew 20:31). They stayed put and got louder. Walking away would have been the easy way out, and they didn't take it.
Yes, baker. "Jesus stopped and called them" (Matthew 20:32). A big crowd was moving along, and He stopped for two men sitting by the road. I think that tells you plenty about who gets His attention.
Not here, friend. Matthew says, "Jesus stopped and called them" (Matthew 20:32). He didn't pass by. These two had been shouting that He was passing by, and He stopped.

explanations.answer: He sends a disciple to hush them
explanations.explanation: That was the crowd's move, baker, not His. The crowd admonished them to be silent (Matthew 20:31). But Jesus "stopped and called them" (Matthew 20:32). Nobody got sent to shush anybody.

That's right. "Lord," they answered, "let our eyes be opened" (Matthew 20:33). Jesus had just asked, "What do you want Me to do for you?" (Matthew 20:32), and they knew exactly what to say. No hemming, no hawing. They had their order ready.

Good guess, friend, but their ears were doing fine. Hearing is how they knew Jesus was passing by (Matthew 20:30). What they asked for was, "let our eyes be opened" (Matthew 20:33). The ears had already done their job.
Hearts matter, baker, but that's not what they asked for. They answered, "Lord, let our eyes be opened" (Matthew 20:33). It was a plain request, and they said it straight to Jesus.
Close, but no waiting period here, baker. The text says, "at once they received their sight" (Matthew 20:34). Nothing about a few days. No second visit, no follow-up appointment.
Correct, baker. Matthew 20:34 says, "at once they received their sight." There was no waiting. Jesus touched their eyes, and they could see right then.

That's right, baker. Matthew 20:34 says they "received their sight and followed Him." The first thing they did with their new eyes was walk behind Jesus. I think I'd have stared at my own hands for an hour first.
Not this time, friend. Jericho was the city the crowd was leaving (Matthew 20:29). The text says they "received their sight and followed Him" (Matthew 20:34). They kept going with Jesus.

That's a fair guess, baker, since Jesus once told a healed man to show himself to the priest (Matthew 8:4). But Matthew 20:34 says nothing like that here. These two "received their sight and followed Him."
